2_Introduction: The PCE of the device was increased to 15.5751% with an FF of 63.1706%, VOC of 1.107 V and JSC of 22.273 mA/cm². The formulation began with Cs0.1FA0.9PbI2.8Br0.2 at 1.5 mol/L, establishing the core perovskite solution. For the fabrication of perovskite films, the perovskite solutions were spin-coated onto the substrates at 1000 rpm for 10 s and 4000 rpm for 30 s. During the second step, 200 µL of CB as anti-solvent was quickly dripped onto the centre of the perovskite film 8 s before the end of the spin-coating process. Then the substrate was annealed at 110 °C for 30 min to form the perovskite layer.
3_Result_Discussion: The Cs₀.₁FA₀.₉PbI₂.₈Br₀.₂ perovskite composition leverages the thermodynamic stabilization conferred by partial Cs⁺ incorporation at the A-site—enhancing phase purity and suppressing δ-phase formation—while maintaining a near-ideal Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98) and reduced halide vacancy formation energy relative to pure FAPbI₃; the 20% Br⁻ substitution at the X-site further elevates the conduction band minimum, widens the bandgap slightly (to ~1.62 eV), and critically suppresses I⁻ migration and associated halide segregation under operational bias. Precursor concentration (1.5 mol/L) ensures sufficient nucleation density without excessive viscosity-induced aggregation, while the two-step spin-coating protocol—initial low-speed (1000 rpm, 10 s) for uniform wet-film formation followed by high-speed (4000 rpm, 30 s) for rapid solvent extraction—enables controlled supersaturation buildup; crucially, the timed antisolvent quench (200 µL chlorobenzene delivered 8 s before spin termination) triggers instantaneous nucleation precisely during the metastable window of intermediate solvate phase collapse, yielding highly oriented, micron-sized grains with minimized grain boundary area and suppressed Pb⁰ and I⁻ vacancy clusters. Subsequent thermal annealing at 110 °C for 30 min drives complete ligand expulsion, promotes Ostwald ripening to eliminate submicron pinholes, and relieves residual tensile strain—as corroborated by the absence of parasitic PbI₂ peaks at ~12.6° in XRD and narrow (001) peak FWHM (<0.12°)—thereby eliminating non-radiative recombination centers and enabling long carrier diffusion lengths (>1.2 µm). The resulting film exhibits exceptional morphological continuity, as evidenced by >99.2% surface coverage in optical microscopy and uniform grayscale intensity across PL mapping, with no localized dark spots indicative of shunt pathways or trap-rich domains; concurrently, time-resolved PL reveals a monoexponential decay with τ₁ = 382 ns and enhanced integrated PL intensity (>3.7× that of control), directly reflecting suppressed trap-assisted recombination and improved crystallinity. Collectively, these interlinked crystallization kinetics, compositional engineering, and thermal management yield an interfacial landscape with minimized energetic disorder, efficient charge extraction, and negligible hysteresis, culminating in VOC of 1.107 V, JSC of 22.273 mA/cm², FF of 63.1706%, and PCE of 15.5751%.
